crossRefs.note: I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met…
When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to…
By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.”
When the accusers stood up, they brought no charges against him of such things as I supposed;
but had certain questions against him about their own religion, and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed…
But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined…
But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked…
Moreover, my father, behold, yes, see the skirt of your robe in my hand; for in that I cut off the skirt of your robe…
May Yahweh judge between me and you, and may Yahweh avenge me of you; but my hand will not be on you.
Yahweh, my God, if I have done this, if there is iniquity in my hands,
Pilate therefore went out to them, and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
They answered him, “If this man weren’t an evildoer, we wouldn’t have delivered him up to you.”

translations.web: “Let them therefore”, he said, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”
translations.bsb: So if this man has done anything wrong, let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there.”
translations.kjv: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
translations.asv: Let them therefore, saith he, that are of power among you go down with me, and if there is anything amiss in the man, let them accuse him.
